body.statement: For \(p\geq3\), fixed \(\iota\), and finite \(\Xi\), the procedure terminates after at most \(G_{\#}2^{c_{\max}}+G_{\#}2^{b_{\max}}+(G_{\#}+\binom{G_{\#}}{2})4^{b_{\max}}\) chart or objective leaves and \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\) outward-rounded operations. It rejects \(\rho\notin\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) before covariance or required-well evaluation. A \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) output proves full rank; normalized allocation with \(\rho_j>0\) for every composition row entering the unpooling map; valid chart coverage; positive exact untruncated bounds \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\), \(\kappa_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\kappa_{\mathcal T}\), \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})\geq\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})\), and \(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)\geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)\); positive interiority; the recorded tail and variance bounds; and \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq N_{\max}\). For an empty wrong-graph comparison or remote-pair set, the corresponding exact and certified bounds are \(+\infty\) and impose no numerical check. A \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\) output proves its named obstruction; \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\) makes no substantive claim.
body.justification: This is the proof-producing kernel with distinct global identification, local regularity, and precision outputs.
body.gap: Rump, Kearfott, and Berz--Makino do not jointly propagate Poisson-PGF tails through graph exclusion, global within-graph identification, singular values, covariance, and intervention precision.
body.consumer: It turns a prospective choice of composition, grid, model boxes, and computational budget into an auditable go, stop, or undecided decision.
body.proof_tex:
All loops in \(\mathfrak C\) range over finite graph sets, finite state truncations, finite multi-index tables, finite precision lists, and binary trees of fixed depth.  A binary tree of depth \(d\) has at most \(2^d\) leaves.  Product-box trees are bounded more coarsely by \(4^{b_{\max}}\).  Summing over graph charts, graph objectives, same-graph remote products, and unordered wrong-graph products gives at most
\[
G_{\#}2^{c_{\max}}+G_{\#}2^{b_{\max}}
+\left(G_{\#}+\binom{G_{\#}}2\right)4^{b_{\max}}. \tag{24}
\]
The precision loop has
\[
P_{\mathrm{ar}}=
1+\left\lceil\frac{b_{\mathrm{cap}}-b_0}{\Delta b}\right\rceil
\]
passes.  By the literal operation accounting in
\(\mathrm{def{:}arithmetic\text{-}complexity}\), each pass and leaf uses at most the displayed recurrence cost plus the displayed cubic linear-algebra cost.  Multiplication by the leaf ceiling, including its extra terminal task, is exactly \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\).  This proves termination and both ceilings.

We prove enclosure soundness by induction through the procedure.  For a conditional Poisson variable,
\[
\mathbb E[V_s^m\mid V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)}]
=\sum_{k=0}^m
\left\{\begin{matrix}m\\k\end{matrix}\right\}\lambda_s^k.
\]
For \(h_s=1+|\operatorname{pa}(s)|\), convexity gives
\[
\left(\alpha_s+\sum_u b_{su}V_u^{q_{su}}\right)^k
\leq h_s^{k-1}\left(\alpha_s^k+
\sum_u b_{su}^kV_u^{q_{su}k}\right). \tag{25}
\]
Topological induction proves that every \(U_{\boldsymbol d rs}(m)\) majorizes its corresponding raw moment.  The same proof holds after the intervention deletes one kernel and substitutes a fixed count.

For a multi-index \(\nu\), direct differentiation of a Poisson log mass and the uniform lower rate \(\lambda^-_{rs}>0\) bounds its first derivative by \(L_{e_t}\) and its higher derivatives by \(L_\nu\).  The multivariate Leibniz rule then shows inductively that
\[
|\partial^\nu p_\theta(v)|\leq p_\theta(v)D_\nu(v). \tag{26}
\]
If \(T_R=\{v:\text{some }v_s>R_s\}\), the union bound and
\(\mathbf1\{v_s>R_s\}\leq v_s^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}}/(R_s+1)^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}}\)
give from (26)
\[
\sum_{v\in T_R}|\partial^\nu p_\theta(v)|
\leq\sum_s
\frac{\mathcal U_{\boldsymbol d r}(D_\nu V_s^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}})}
{(R_s+1)^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}}}
=E_{\boldsymbol d r,\nu}. \tag{27}
\]
Multiplication by \(V_{i_Y}+V_{i_Z}\) proves the intervention-contrast version.  The inequality
\[
|ab-\widetilde a\widetilde b|
\leq |a||b-\widetilde b|
+|\widetilde b||a-\widetilde a|
\leq2\varepsilon_0+\varepsilon_0^2
\]
when \(a,b\in[0,1]\) and both errors are at most \(\varepsilon_0\), proves the covariance-product enlargement.

For \(x\geq0\), Taylor's theorem at zero gives
\[
\left|e^{-x}-\sum_{k=0}^{a}\frac{(-x)^k}{k!}\right|
\leq\frac{x^{a+1}}{(a+1)!}, \tag{28}
\]
so the initial exponential interval is valid.  The Poisson recurrence, the complete-Bell recurrence, the multivariate Leibniz recurrence, and the fixed Taylor formula preserve enclosure by induction.  Equation (27) then enlarges retained sums to enclose the exact infinite sums.  Finally, downward rounding of lower endpoints and upward rounding of upper endpoints preserve every exact value under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division whenever the divisor interval excludes zero.  Thus every interval recorded by the procedure contains its exact untruncated target.

A positive lower endpoint for a wrong-graph or remote objective is therefore a valid lower bound for every point in that leaf.  The coverage checks make the passing leaves cover the entire required feasible set, proving
\[
\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T},\quad
\Lambda_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}.
\]
The interval \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) tests certify positive definiteness of
\(J^{\mathsf T}J-u^2I\) and of
\((PJ+J^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T})/2-uI\), proving respectively
\[
\kappa_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\kappa_{\mathcal T}>0,\qquad
\mu_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}>0. \tag{29}
\]
Exact rational endpoint comparisons similarly certify box validity, rank, simplex normalization, positive row masses, interior clearance, covariance denominators, variance upper bounds, and \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq N_{\max}\).  The simplex test is ordered before every covariance and well calculation, proving the stated early rejection.

For a Krawczyk collision test, every Jacobian is enclosed and the cited Krawczyk inclusion theorem gives a zero of the selected square moment difference inside the product box.  Singleton zero enclosures for all omitted coordinates make it a zero of the full moment difference.  Disjoint parameter factors then give a genuine wrong-graph collision.  Exact rank defect, invalid rational boxes, and simplex failure are themselves the other named obstructions.  Therefore every \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\) status proves its recorded obstruction.  By definition no conclusion is attached to an exhausted or failed test, so \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\) is substantively silent.  Empty comparison sets are handled by their declared \(+\infty\) conventions.
